reason: README documents a `da3 auto` CLI on bundled example images; the small Apache-2.0 DA3-SMALL variant runs on CPU with ungated HF weights.
demo: README Quick Start > Basic Usage: `da3 auto assets/examples/SOH --export-format glb --export-dir ... --model-dir ${MODEL_DIR}` (CLI without backend), with the README's DA3-SMALL model on CPU
goal: Install the project from the clone following the README Installation section so the `da3` CLI works on this CPU-only machine. Then `da3 auto assets/examples/SOH --export-format mini_npz-glb --export-dir <a new directory> --model-dir depth-anything/DA3-SMALL --device cpu` must finish and write results.npz and scene.glb into the export dir; DA3-SMALL is the README's smallest Apache-2.0 model and downloads from Hugging Face without a token. Put any environment activation in /work/env.sh.
check: The hidden test runs that command into a fresh export dir and verifies the npz depth/confidence/camera arrays have the right shapes for the 2 images and that scene.glb holds a non-trivial point cloud.

revision.by: second review (outside the maintained set; independent log check of maintained passes)
issues: Oracle bug: it pre-creates the export dir with mktemp -d and passes it as --export-dir; da3 then asks 'Export directory ... already exists. Do you want to clean it and continue? [y/N]' and aborts without a tty. This, not the repo, failed the main run.

Oracle omits --device cpu although the CLI defaults to device='cuda'; a correct README install on a CPU box cannot pass, which pushed the agent into patching services/inference_service.py (counted in repo_diff).
Goal leaks an install hint: 'gsplat/xformers are not needed'. xformers is a hard dependency in pyproject.toml and the README installs it explicitly; the goal should not tell the agent to drop it.
Coverage widened: v2 also checks conf/extrinsics/intrinsics shapes and that scene.glb holds a real point cloud.
